# `seo` — module reference

Rendered from the module's own manifest, and from nothing written by hand. What the module *does* is [its own page](../modules/seo.md).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Module id | `seo` |
| Name | SEO |
| Version | `1.0.0` |
| Ships from | `@endora-commerce/mod-seo` |

## Activation

An operator switches this module on and off on **/platform/modules**. The choice is the setting `seo.enabled`, and it defaults to **on**.

## Dependencies

| Module | Binding | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth` | yes | installs and migrates after it, and an operator cannot switch it off underneath this module |
| `catalog` | yes | installs and migrates after it, and an operator cannot switch it off underneath this module |
| `cms` | yes | installs and migrates after it, and an operator cannot switch it off underneath this module |
